rationale: The golden solution, which correctly implements the pinned interface (synchronous write with synchronous active-high reset, purely combinational reads with inherent write-forwarding), is rejected by evaluate.py on FR1, FR3, and FR4 due to a harness bug: the testbench fails to emit a PROBE line for cycle 0, producing 'missing PROBE for cycle 0' / 'missing PROBE for collision cycle 0' errors rather than an actual behavioral mismatch. This is a clean stimulus/probe-timing defect in tb_regfile.v (a delta-cycle or $fscanf/array-indexing bug dropping the first probe), not a cycle-offset disagreement between two independently authored designs — the golden's own METRICS show cycle_accurate_match_rate=0.995, i.e. only the first cycle's probe is lost, confirming a harness bug rather than a genuine timing mismatch rooted in an underspecified interface. Because the golden run fails preflight, mutation testing is blocked entirely (mutation_status=blocked_by_differential, mutation_score=0.0 not meaningful, discrimination_coverage=0.0). The vulnerable/naive baseline is also contaminated by the same probe-loss bug (its failures start at cycle 1, distinct from golden's cycle-0 failures) — coincidentally it still fails, but for an unreliable/wrong reason, so evaluator behavior cannot be trusted. Analyzer and validation reports agree the golden_rejected issue is the primary defect, and this squarely maps to the golden_rejected repair path.
revision_instructions: evaluate.py rejects a correct golden submission with '[TEST] FAIL: FR1: missing PROBE for cycle 0', '[TEST] FAIL: FR3: missing PROBE for collision cycle 0', and '[TEST] FAIL: FR4: missing PROBE for cycle 0' — these are harness-emission bugs, not genuine behavioral mismatches (the same golden design's own METRICS line shows cycle_accurate_match_rate=0.995, i.e. only the very first PROBE is being dropped). Fix evaluation/tb_regfile.v (and any evaluate.py glue that parses its PROBE output) so that a PROBE line is reliably emitted for cycle 0 of every scenario, including the very first write/read cycle and the very first collision cycle — inspect the stimulus-loading loop, any array/index-based drive sequencing, and delta-cycle ordering between applying stimulus and sampling outputs at time 0; ensure the probe-and-compare step for cycle 0 runs unconditionally before any other cycles are processed, with no dependency on a prior iteration having executed. After the fix, every FR/SR check must grade PASS/FAIL purely from simulated observed behavior (compiled and run via iverilog/vvp against the pinned reg_file_recovered port list) — never by requiring a specific PROBE count or any source-text property, since a differently-structured but behaviorally correct submission must still pass. Re-run the differential test and confirm the golden submission passes all 7 requirements (FR1-FR4, SR1-SR3) with exit code 0, and that the naive/empty baseline still fails FR1/FR3/FR4 for genuine behavioral reasons (not the probe-loss artifact). Once fixed, re-run mutation testing to obtain a meaningful discrimination coverage score, since it is currently blocked at 0.0.
